```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(phwstyle)
# The phw_* formats already call use_phw_ggplot() and use_phw_flextable(),
# so every chart and flextable below is styled. Add theme_phw() or a
# scale_*_phw_*() to a plot only to change something for that plot.
# Optional: keep group colours the same in every report.
# phw_key_file("phw-colours.csv")
```

# Summary

This report uses the Public Health Wales house style automatically: Ubuntu
type, navy headings, PHW chart colours and booktabs tables.

> A key message goes here, in a highlighted box.

# Section heading

```{r chart, fig.cap = "Figure caption describing the chart", fig.alt = "Bar chart of the value for each year from 2016 to 2025. It falls from 118 in 2016 to 73 in 2025."}
d <- tibble(year = 2016:2025, value = c(118, 104, 104, 98, 96, 78, 82, 75, 89, 73))
ggplot(d, aes(year, value)) +
  geom_col(fill = phw_col("navy")) +
  geom_text(aes(label = value), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = d$year) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Value", caption = phw_caption("Example data"))
```

```{r table}
tbl <- tibble(Area = paste("Area", LETTERS[1:7]),
              `Year 1` = c(4.4, 0.7, 4.2, 0.2, 1.6, 3.0, 3.7),
              `Year 2` = c(2.0, 2.0, 5.5, 2.3, 2.6, 0.7, 3.9))
phw_flextable(tbl, caption = "Table caption", source = "Example data", bold_first_col = TRUE)
```
